definitions.scope: campaigns with 1,000 or more contestants whose organizer site was labelled (the 100 to 1,000 band now has counts from the contestant dump and appears in field_cuts.by_band_all). Campaigns run from a shared platform host (youtube, twitch, twitter and so on) carry a per-campaign industry from their own names and a business type from the host, and only those still unlabelled are excluded
definitions.conversion: contestants over impressions, all runs, so long and repeatable campaigns sit lower
definitions.email_uptake: email entries per contestant in campaigns offering the action
definitions.labels: industry and business type from the organizer homepage and campaign names, assistant labelled, plus platform markers from the homepage HTML
definitions.enrichment: org_scale from Tranco rank, Wikidata and Apollo revenue, employees and listing; ap_* fields, employee and founded bands, funding stage and marketing stack from Apollo organization enrichment; org_stage, niche and audience from a second assistant pass over the homepage text; youtube_band from channel subscriber counts; shop_* from the Shopify storefront JSON. Every group needs at least five distinct organizers, so no row describes one company
definitions.channel_size_within_industry: the channel's action-join size band (youtube subscribers, discord members, telegram members) crossed with the campaign's homepage industry, so a raw size gap that is really an industry effect (crypto and Telegram, gaming and Discord) can be told apart from one that holds inside an industry. Ten distinct organizers required per cell, not five, because this is finer than a plain industry cut
definitions.channel_size_within_contestant_band: channel size band crossed with the campaign's own contestant band (100-250, 250-500, 500-1k, 1k-2.5k, 2.5k-10k, 10k+), the more direct control: at the same campaign size, does a bigger channel convert better or draw more entries per entrant
definitions.channel_size_predicts_campaign_size: a log-log regression of valid_contestants on the raw channel-size number (not the band) for youtube subscribers, discord members and telegram members. slope near 0 means channel size barely moves campaign size once you look continuously rather than by band; r_squared shows how much of the spread it actually explains
definitions.youtube_subscribers_vs_views_per_video: subscriber band crossed with views-per-video band (total channel views over video count), a rough engagement-per-subscriber proxy independent of raw subscriber count
definitions.youtube_subscribers_vs_channel_age: subscriber band crossed with whether the channel was created 2017 or later versus earlier, to see whether an older channel with a modest subscriber count behaves like a young channel at the same count or like a bigger channel
definitions.channel_size_vs_direct_traffic: direct_share is the median share of a campaign's landing-page impressions with no referrer (locations.direct), by the organizer's channel size band. A channel-size effect here would show organizers with bigger channels pulling more of their own direct or app traffic rather than referred clicks

vertical_mapping.note: the earlier verticals came from a title regex; the second dataset uses homepage labels. On the same scope both give gaming about 27 to 28% conversion, so the published 36% was the clean ordinary subset of the earlier dataset, not a label difference
